question: What additional historical river/lake and later population-study sources can be verified for the Ormoc Lake Danao catchment, and what can they safely contribute without double-counting?

riverAndOutlet: Inawasan River (described by the 2007 paper as the outlet of Tubod River)
waterbodyCluster.identityBoundary: Keep this Ormoc City, Leyte cluster separate from the Lake Danao on Pacijan Island, Cebu; Polangui, Albay; and the Balinsasayao Twin Lakes Natural Park, Negros Oriental.
waterbodyCluster.geometryDecision: No coordinates or polygons added. The 2007 public abstract supplies no sampling stations, while the 2023 and 2025 papers use a single study-area locator and no station-level fish geometry.

historicalGuide2007.citation: Weliange, W. S., Pogosa, J., Lankaadikara, C., Leichtfried, M., & Goltenboth, F. (2007). Guide to the fresh water fishes in Tubod River, Lake Dnao and Inawasan River in Leyte, Philippines. Annals of Tropical Research, 29(2), 1-27. https://doi.org/10.32945/atr2921.2007.
historicalGuide2007.abstractLevelEvidence: The official VSU abstract describes an identification guide for 21 freshwater fish species, reporting 18 in Tubod River and one in its outlet Inawasan River. It does not provide the species-by-site list or allocate the remaining two species in the abstract; Lake Danao is named in the article title.
historicalGuide2007.fullTextStatus: Official landing page and abstract verified. The linked 27-page PDF did not successfully render/retrieve in this review, so no table, individual species, voucher, or site assignment was extracted.
historicalGuide2007.secondaryCrossCitation: The 2023 NFRDI paper cites Weliange et al. (2007) in support of its historical Lake Danao statements for Cyprinus carpio and Clarias batrachus. Because the original species-by-site text and specimen details were not inspectable here, preserve those as citations reported by the 2023 paper, not as independently checked 2007 species rows.
historicalGuide2007.reuse: The VSU journal page shows CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. No article text, species descriptions or figures were copied; Bangwit reuse and ShareAlike compatibility remain unreviewed.

laterStudy2025.citation: Gaut, M. N. P. C., Romero, J. B., Dañal, R. M. S., Cabansag, J. B. P., & de la Cruz, J. O. (2025). Growth, mortality, and exploitation rate of Glossogobius giuris (Hamilton, 1822) in Lake Danao Natural Park, Ormoc City (Philippines). Limnology and Freshwater Biology, 5, 1119-1128. https://doi.org/10.31951/2658-3518-2025-A-5-1119.
laterStudy2025.sampleEvidence: The article reports 867 Glossogobius giuris from landed catch, sampled bi-monthly from March 2021 through February 2022 using local fishers' handlines and small-mesh fishing nets. The 2025 paper's author list overlaps the 2023 assemblage paper in Romero, Dañal and de la Cruz; the date window overlaps the earlier study's catch window.
laterStudy2025.relationshipTo2023: Sample dependence is plausible because of shared authors, location, and overlapping collection dates, but no specimen-level identifier or explicit data crosswalk proves how many individual fish overlap. Retain both paper records and do not add 867 to the 1,462 catch total or treat the 2025 article as a second independent occurrence survey.
laterStudy2025.spatialAndBiologicalLimits: The paper reports one locator coordinate for the study area, not station-level occurrences. It does not report voucher catalogue numbers. Its discussion's diet information cites external work and the 2023 article, rather than presenting a new Lake Danao gut-content study.
laterStudy2025.reuse: The paper states CC BY-NC 4.0. Only limited methodological and cross-study facts are recorded; no tables, figures or raw size data were copied, and no Bangwit publication approval is recorded.

projectOutputLead.project: Fisheries and Biodiversity Resources Assessment and Monitoring in Lake Danao (FiBRe), within the LAKES Danao program.
projectOutputLead.period: 1 October 2020-30 September 2022 according to the NRCP/DOST project record.
projectOutputLead.statusConflict: The NRCP page still displays Ongoing, while the UP Tacloban research-project listing marks the program Completed. Neither page supplied raw fish records, a final fish checklist, vouchers or a report link in the reviewed listing.
projectOutputLead.nextResearchAction: Check public institutional repositories for a final FiBRe report and voucher catalog numbers; if still unavailable, leave the source gap explicit. No email or access request was sent.

limitations: The 2007 article's full species list, methods, vouchers, site assignments and primary record details were not retrievable in this pass; the abstract is not enough to populate a waterbody inventory.
The 2023 and 2025 Lake Danao catch datasets have overlapping periods and shared authors. They remain distinct publications, but sample-level independence is unknown.
Historical study-area evidence does not establish current fish presence, population status, abundance, legal catchability, safety, bait effectiveness or complete lake/river coverage.
The project listing discrepancy and absence of public outputs do not establish that records do not exist; only that none were exposed in the pages reviewed.
No species assertion, catch event, current-presence record, geometry, origin label, diet claim, rules or safety advice was changed or added.
nextAction: Search official UP Tacloban, UP Visayas, DOST-NRCP, Visayas State University and public catalog records for the completed FiBRe report, 2007 guide species-by-site table and any UPTC/UPV voucher accessions. Continue the Eastern Visayas lake-and-river sweep only from records with inspectable waterbody attribution and source terms.
